Implement a hierarchical optimal coordination control layer on the locomotive's Electronic Control Pneumatic (ECP) or brake control unit. This layer replaces the current fixed-step deceleration logic with a Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) combined with a feedforward-robust integral sliding mode tracker. The objective is to compute a smooth, optimal expected deceleration profile that maintains traction-adhesion margins during emergency braking on contaminated rails, thereby preventing wheel-lock sliding and flat spotting.

PARAMETER: PSO swarm size (N_particles) — 30 particles — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: LQR weight matrix ratio (Q/R) — 100/1 (acceleration penalty vs. control effort) — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Maximum allowable longitudinal jerk (j_max) — 0.5 m/s³ — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Time-To-Collision pre-estimation horizon (T_TTC) — 3.0 s — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Wheel-slip threshold for intervention (s_threshold) — 0.10 (dimensionless) — ASSUMPTION
PARAMETER: Adhesion coefficient estimate for contaminated rail (μ_contam) — 0.25 — ASSUMPTION

The system monitors wheel speed and axle speed to calculate slip. When slip exceeds s_threshold, the PSO-LQR layer activates, calculating a deceleration profile that maximizes braking force while keeping slip below the threshold. The sliding mode tracker ensures smooth execution, avoiding the sudden changes in deceleration that cause longitudinal jerk and wheel locking. This approach respects the existing EN braking distance standard by ensuring the total stopping distance remains within limits, while reducing the incidence of wheel flats. No track infrastructure changes are required; the intervention is purely software/firmware on the locomotive's existing brake control hardware.

Expected measurable effect: A 40% reduction in wheel flat incidence per 10,000 emergency braking events on contaminated rails, with braking distance variance reduced by 15% compared to current systems.

Falsification test:
- Test temperature: 20 °C ambient (standard test track conditions)
- Duration: 2 weeks of operational monitoring on a 50-km contaminated rail segment
- Sample size n: 1,000 emergency braking events
- Numeric pass/fail criteria: Pass if the mean wheel-slip peak is < 0.15 AND the frequency of flat spotting events is reduced by > 30% relative to baseline; fail if braking distance exceeds the EN standard limit by > 5% OR if flat spotting frequency shows no significant reduction (p > 0.05).

Evidence support: The control strategy is based on autonomous emergency braking optimal coordination control strategies, which propose improved Time-To-Collision pre-estimation models and state threshold time determination to solve sudden changes in expected braking deceleration. Note: This specific parameterization for freight locomotives is UNVERIFIED and requires the stated test to confirm efficacy.
